author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Test PS2 audio with Android sound enhancements disabled
summary: Capture Android audio processing, disable one enhancement at a time, compare the same PS2 passage at matched volume, and distinguish route processing from emulation speed.
heroAlt: Tomb Raider scene used as a controlled speech, music, and effects passage while Android sound processing is compared

blocks.text: Bypass Android processing without moving the emulator target
Determine whether spatial audio, equalization, loudness normalization, vendor effects, or accessibility processing introduces distortion or imbalance.
Disabling every audio feature at once can improve the result but leaves no evidence about the responsible processor.

items: System and vendor audio-effect panels photographed.
Playback volume fixed below clipping level.
Same output device retained for all comparisons.

blocks.text: Remove one processor and replay the same passage

items: 1. Record the active equalizer, spatial, normalization, and accessibility effects.
2. Play the chosen passage and note exact timestamps of the symptom.
3. Disable only the first enhancement and restart the audio route if required.
4. Replay at matched volume and record whether the artifact changes.
5. Restore that effect before testing the next processor.
6. Compare a second PS2 title using the same route and volume.
7. Test the clean path during both full-speed and slow emulation.
8. Retain only the smallest documented system change that improves both passes.

blocks.text: A true enhancement fault follows the Android processor across games, while emulation-speed audio faults follow workload and timing even on a clean route.
The clean comparison identifies one processing layer or proves enhancements are not responsible, with safe volume and stable routing.

items: Only one Android processor changes between paired samples.
Volume is matched closely enough to avoid a louder-is-better judgment.
The conclusion holds across route restart and a second title.

blocks.text: Results that point outside enhancement processing

items: Crackle appears only below full speed: diagnose performance or audio buffering.
Artifact follows one headset: inspect its codec or hardware.
Every configuration clips at maximum volume: lower gain before comparison.
One game passage alone sounds odd: select a confirmed reference scene.

blocks.text: Restore each recorded enhancement and volume value after preserving the accepted comparison.
Effect names and availability vary by vendor
Two phones can expose different Dolby, spatial, EQ, or hearing features; record the exact build and do not prescribe a missing vendor toggle.
Use Android low-latency audio guidance for the clean path
